point_of_contention: Do the chapter-local defects filed under this topic stand unrebutted - a Reveling benefit still settled in commercial terms after the currency was retired, and a raw-Typst block opened on line 3 that nothing ever closes?
ruling: Both defects are established and the council must carry them: the Reveling benefit must be restated in the book's grant vocabulary as earned or granted with no price attached, and the chapter's raw-Typst block must be terminated by a closing fence.
reasoning: Three refutes are filed here and not one is challenged, rebutted or defended against anywhere in the brief, so both defects stand as presented. The commerce refutes locate the funding verb and the priced night inside the mechanic itself, note that the book defines no coin, no inn tariff and no revel allowance, and show the chapter's own titles sentence two clauses away already models the granted-not-bought phrasing, so the repair is confined to the Reveling sentence. The build refute reports a fresh render of the current tree reproducing the stain at pages 291-293 on pages carrying no monospace face, and shows that appending a single closing fence, changing nothing else, yields decorated headings and two genuine tables; it also identifies the repository gate that counts opening fences without ever testing for a closer, which is why the defect passed. The arithmetic counters in the same findings report the chapter's numbers independently recomputed and clean, so nothing in the record cuts against either defect.
conditions: The commerce repair is confined to the Reveling sentence: the chapter's titles sentence already models the granted-not-bought phrasing, and the token scan in the filed evidence finds no coin unit printed elsewhere in the chapter.

The arithmetic the refutes recomputed clean - the 32-point DP total, the tier prices at 2/4/8, the tier gates, the absent retired damage row and the reputation bands - must not be reopened by this repair.

The fence repair must be accepted only on a clean rebuild showing decorated section headings and both ladders as real tables; the repository's fence gate that counts openers without testing for a closer does not evidence the block is sound.

A wording-only repair to Reveling leaves the award's magnitude and any bound on it untouched; that question is filed under the reputation topic and must remain open rather than treated as closed by this ruling.

point_of_contention: Do the reputation defects stand - an automatic, uncapped carousing point that is the cheapest printed route up the standing ladder, and an advertised standing-to-title eligibility that nothing in the book implements?
ruling: Both reputation defects stand and the council must carry them: the carousing award cannot ship as an automatic, uncapped point and must be given a printed bound (a level link, a per-arc cap, or DA assignment), and the advertised title eligibility must be closed by either deleting the promise from the reputation opening or naming the required standing inside the titles rule.
reasoning: The faucet refute prices the mechanic exactly - each hero one carousing night per session, a flat point rather than a DA-assigned value, no ceiling on the ladder above the top band - and shows the defect is load-bearing: the deeds that are supposed to drive renown print no point figure while the loss rule strips a whole band, so a free repeatable social action outranks the heroics it is meant to reward. The eligibility refute shows the promised gate has no implementer anywhere: every rung of the standing ladder awards recognition, hospitality, a following or lasting fame and never a title, the titles rule makes the deed the test and attaches no standing threshold, and the term list carries no such headword. The round-two re-test could not break either finding; it only tightened the arithmetic, conceding the points are not strictly irreversible and reporting the strict single-point reading as crossing on night fourteen rather than fifteen. Nothing in the brief defends either mechanic.
conditions: The filed fifteen-session crossing is an outer bound: counted strictly as one point per session from the ladder's own floor of one, the top band first lands on night fourteen, and any restatement must use the corrected figure.
The gain is one point while the setback rule removes a whole band, so the points are not strictly irreversible; no repair may rest on the contrary assumption.
Any meter must be printed in the chapter: a DA-assigned value or a cap the text never authorises does not repair the defect.
The mapping between this party reputation scale and the guide's separate faction scale is not established by anything in the arguments and must not be invented in order to close the title gap.

point_of_contention: Do this topic's two defects stand - a milestone label that names a benefit the defining chapter calls a discipline rank, and a title example that hands over an Adept-tier card with no level floor - and is the repair a narrow wording fix or a redesign of the reward section?
ruling: Both defects stand and must be repaired narrowly in place: the milestone label must be restated in the rank vocabulary the defining chapter and the glossary use, with a cross-reference to the chapter that owns the grant, and the title example's card grant must carry its tier's level requirement; any remedy that treats the reward section as unplayable or as needing redesign is rejected.
reasoning: On the label, the filed refute shows the term is defined nowhere - the chapter offers no pointer, the defining chapter and the glossary speak only of ranks and tiers, and the quick-reference sheet repeats the same name at the same three levels - and the round-two tally classifies the cell as misnamed rather than under-specified, so the correction is vocabulary, not new design. On the card, the round-one premise that the book admits no route to a card except purchase was broken by the round-two challenge, which cites ancestry gifts carrying the tier ladder without Discipline prerequisites, item-granted ranks that feed prerequisites like bought ranks, and a level-caveated faction-favour precedent, and which bounds the stake at a single four-DP card granted once. That challenge does not reach the defect: every canon statement quoted ties the level requirement to the card's tier, the book's one stated waiver expressly keeps level requirements in force, the nearest gift idiom drops only Discipline prerequisites, and the only free-card precedent outside cantrips sits at the lowest tier. A granted card therefore inherits its tier floor, and the title example prints no floor and no waiver - a one-line omission, which is why the redesign inference of the round-one finding is rejected while the defect it identified is kept.
conditions: The rename must land in both files: the chapter's own gains column at levels 3, 6 and 9, and the identical milestone mirror on the quick-reference sheet.
A rename alone leaves the reader without a pointer; the chapter must cross-reference the chapter that defines the grant, since its only existing pointer returns the reader to the same table.
Whether a granted card is held outright or lapses with the title is not settled by the arguments and needs explicit wording; it must not be assumed either way.
Whether a title may waive a card's tier floor is a new rule with no support in the record; it must not be written in as part of this repair.
This ruling leaves the chapter-local reward defects and the reputation ladder defects as separate matters under their own topics; it closes neither.
